title: Speed up pinned E8 replay with shared prefixes and exact admission
body:
The pinned PR358 native pipeline recomputes producer prefixes across six consumers and spends substantial proof time on rational arithmetic and transcript bookkeeping. This packages the tested external adapters into one portable, source-pinned contribution: share freshly computed prefixes in isolated fork children, accelerate exact predecessor/scalar arithmetic, and overlap independent native work with the same two stage workers.

A fresh sequential A/B of the relocated package took **285.41 → 164.88 seconds (42.23% less wall time, 1.73× speedup)**. Total process-tree CPU fell **29.57%**. Both configurations start from the same two-worker driver; this measures the accumulated optimizations, not scalar admission alone. One CPython3.13.12 macOS pair; OS caches were not flushed. Runtime/compiler details and compact comparison evidence are included.

Validation:
- All **29 focused tests** and **24 full native stages** pass. All839 frozen upstream Git blobs remain exact before/after both runs.
- **49 artifacts** match byte-for-byte;34 producer files match (gzip payloads decompressed),15 predecessor receipts agree after timing/path normalization, and all fresh receipt hash bindings are independently revalidated before comparison.
- Clean scalar proof packing changes24→16 bits under the same freshly computed residual bound and strict radix inequality. All eleven corruption controls retain the original24 bits. The exact argument and the two intentionally changed receipt fields are documented.
- Final word, finite invoice, prices, refinement and conditional κ are unchanged. Preserve the external-execution sidecars with optimized receipts.

`research/e8-replay-performance/README.md` is the review/reproduction map. The package is about0.5MB; explicit acquisition fetches only the839 pinned PR358 blobs (36MB), while source caches, compilers and generated replay outputs are excluded from Git. Replay and tests are offline after acquisition. Dedicated path-filtered CI repeats tests and the complete sequential A/B, without enforcing a noisy timing threshold. CI is not claimed passed before it runs.

The historical scalar-only A/B (baseline already using the other optimizations) remains separately labeled:35.7% less scalar time,2.6% less full-pipeline time, with increased scalar-child peak RSS. No measurement of latest-frontier pipelines or community discovery throughput is claimed. This remains a POSIX fork prototype and retains every inherited all-size/analytic assumption; no new κ or unconditional theorem.

Independent branch from main; PR367 remains focused on exact frame algebra and is not a dependency. Prepared by Aman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; upstream authorship, Apache-2.0 licenses, notices and assistance disclosures are retained.
